a: 301 Moved Permanently means the resource has a new permanent URL.
304 Not Modified means the client can use its cached copy.
400 Bad Request means the server could not understand the request.
401 Unauthorized means authentication is required or failed.
403 Forbidden means the server understood but refuses access.
404 Not Found means no resource at that path.
405 Method Not Allowed means that HTTP method is not supported for the resource.
500 Internal Server Error is a generic server-side failure.
503 Service Unavailable means the server is temporarily overloaded or down.
